svg.title: Day 3 after a crush injury. 58-year-old man, oliguric. Creatinine has risen from 0.9 to 2.1 mg/dL over two days. Potassium 6.4 mEq/L. ECG shows tall, peaked T waves. He reports muscle weakness, incision pain 6 of 10, and has a temperature of 38.1 °C. BP 132/78, HR 58, RR 18.
svg.desc: Pain and a low-grade fever are real competing problems, but a potassium of 6.4 mEq/L with peaked T waves has already reached the heart, so monitoring and membrane stabilization come first. IV calcium does not lower potassium; it protects the myocardium while insulin, binders, or dialysis remove it. Giving potassium is the trap for anyone who reads the number as low. Reported normal ranges differ by laboratory, roughly 3.5 to 5.0 or 3.7 to 5.2 mEq/L, but 6.4 is high on any of them.
